items.claim: Define a selected finite-regulator model's physical 2-group symmetry action, coupled finite background cochains, field/observable assignments, counterterm scheme, and physical scope.
source_uses: Benini, Córdova and Hsin §2.3, printed pp. 18–20 / PDF pp. 19–21: finite 2-group backgrounds and gauge transformations.
Schäfer-Nameki §§2.5, 2.8.1, printed pp. 23–32: higher-form backgrounds, 2-group symmetry data and Postnikov constraint.
items.disposition: Complete selected finite-regulator model definition with explicit field, action, measure, observable, symmetry, background, gauge-arrow, counterterm and physical-scope data. The p-form and topological-defect interfaces and all four batch-13 cochain/groupoid inputs were inspected and have current-ready Step 1 records; every stated convention matches the consumer use. This is an authoring readiness check, not independent proof approval.

items.claim: For a selected finite-regulator model with coherent gauge-arrow bijections and an explicitly specified field-independent phase in its weight transformation, derive the induced partition-function and unnormalized-correlator variation, and state exactly how allowed local counterterms change that phase.
source_uses: Benini, Córdova and Hsin §3 introduction, printed pp. 20–21 / PDF pp. 21–22: anomaly as a background-gauge phase modulo local counterterms; §§1.2–1.3: Postnikov datum is background structure.
Schäfer-Nameki §2.8.2, printed p. 33: gauging can induce a mixed anomaly, so the distinction is not a claim of physical independence.
items.disposition: Complete conditional finite-sum change-of-variables proof from the adopted model weight/observable law and the coherent finite background groupoid. All direct suppliers are present, current-ready and interface-matched. The theorem assigns no phase to an unspecified model, identifies no anomaly from beta alone, and asserts no continuum limit.

Schäfer-Nameki §2.5, printed pp. 23–25: discrete higher-form backgrounds and gauge equivalence.
items.disposition: The split Z2 background equation, edge-gauge face values and unit response are verified by explicit finite calculation on the closed triangulation. All direct suppliers are present, current-ready and interface-matched; the response is an adopted model input, with no continuum or empirical claim.

items.claim: Verify a Z2-valued normalized nonzero Postnikov class and a background/gauge transform on a closed triangulated 3-sphere for which the selected unit-weight response has no gauge phase.
source_uses: Benini, Córdova and Hsin §2.3 and §1.3: Postnikov background equation and its distinction from an anomaly.
Schäfer-Nameki §§2.8.1–2.8.2: Postnikov class and its relation to anomalies only through a specified model/gauging operation.
items.disposition: The normalized cocycle, non-coboundary witness, global background equation and transformed tetrahedron are verified by explicit Z2 calculations. All direct suppliers are present, current-ready and interface-matched; the unit response is an adopted finite-model input and no general anomaly conclusion follows.
